decisions: Runs after scenario.json, on the module scenario.json creates. The check predicted champion_loadout.py at 456 rendered lines; black re-wraps the tool's one-line imports and the file landed at 503, three over the ceiling, and sightline reported the size arm on a module that was extracted to clear it. A file-length marker is not available to a new module, so one more unit leaves.

The unit that leaves is the ability-rank pair. _ability_max_rank reads a kit's authored rank cardinality and _validate_ability_ranks accepts or refuses the ranks a roster card asks for at a level; that is a question about the request, not about the card, and it is the same question fight_request_bounds.rank_allocation_contract answers for allocation mode. Its own file is the honest home until the two can share one: extract_modules.py moves units out of one source, and those two live in different sources.
ability_ranks.py is a leaf on champions.skill_orders alone and champion_loadout drops to 453 rendered lines.

modules.docstring: How many ranks a kit authored, and the ranks a roster card may ask for at a level.
